newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Mediocre demand flattens SE Asian prices.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Mediocre demand flattens SE Asian prices.

text.p: Flat demand will keep Southeast Asian rubber prices on the defensive this week with Thai government buying the only factor shoring up prices in the market, regional traders said on Monday.

"There's nothing bullish going on. Demand remains mediocre," the senior rubber trader of a North American rubber trading house told Reuters. "I can't say we'll get much relief this week. It's a slow-moving bear market."
"I don't think the market can turn around (this) week. It may consolidate after falls (last) week," said a trader with a Malaysian firm. "There's still very poor demand from consumers."

Traders did not rule out the possibility of a further price retreat, especially with wintering almost over in some areas. The approach of the Easter holidays in major consumers like the United States and Europe may also dampen sentiment.
"The market looks quite low, but it's difficult to predict. It can go lower given the lack of demand," a dealer in Malaysia said.
"Wintering is already over in a few areas and this can only be bad for stocks and prices," a dealer for a foreign rubber trading firm in Singapore said.

The only feature seen in the market was continued Thai buying for RSS3 grade rubber, which has helped shore up prices. The Thais bought 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 rubber and were still keen on purchasing another 7,000 tonnes.
But Bangkok's purchases may soon run out of steam, the dealers said.
One trader in Thailand said "prices won't be supported for (as) long as real demand is sluggish."
"Japan seemed to slow down buying a bit, perhaps due to their book closing. And the lower prices in Indonesia also make it tougher to attract buyers at the moment," the trader added.
"The Thai government is trying its best to hold prices," another dealer said.
The benchmark RSS3 for April delivery was indicated at 123.00-124.00 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok last Friday from 123.00 cents the previous week, dealers said.
May was indicated at 123.00-124.50 cents on the same basis compared with 123.00-124.00 cents previously. Latex was unchanged at 94 cents a kg.
Malaysian traders, on the other hand, said local producers were also being hard-pressed to match the much lower prices on offer from Indonesia.
They said there had been inquiries for rubber but most of them did not translate into deals.
Small parcels were done on Friday. They included SMR L to Dubai at 332 Malaysian cents a kg, SMR 10 to Britain at 285 cents and SMR 20 to South Korea at 287 cents, all for April delivery.
The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the benchmark April RSS 1 at 300.50 cents a kg last Friday, down from 305.50 cents the previous week.
April SMR 20 was at 287.50 cents against 293 previously. Drum latex was offered at 236 cents a kg.
In Indonesia, traders said they did not expect any significant movement in prices of the benchmark SIR20 this week because of similarly poor demand.
"We expect the market to continue to be dull next week because we don't see any factors which can boost sentiment," said one trader.
SIR20 for April/May shipment was done at 50.00 U.S. cents/lb FOB Palembang. Traders said offer prices firmed at 51.00 FOB, but were seen in Surabaya at 51.00 cents.
In Palembang, offer prices were quoted at 50.75 cents/lb and at 50.50 FOB Pontianak and Jambi. In Padang, offer prices were quoted at 50.75 cents.
Many traders in Medan have said they were not willing to sell at 50.50 cents because it would not be profitable.
"The main question is the absence of buyers and you see how low the prices are in Medan despite the wintering period," said one trader.
"The way it's going, it's not a healthy market," a Singapore-based dealer said.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
